aw (water activity): how much water is free for bacteria.

Water-phase salt (WPS): the salt dissolved in the water of the product, in %.
WPS = NaCl / (NaCl + water) × 100.
This is what counts, not the salt on the total weight.

pH: how acid the product is.
The lower it is, the less Listeria grows.

LAB (lactic acid bacteria): i batteri la:
LAB: lactic acid bacteria.
They carry out the fermentation and, when there are many, they slow Listeria.
Effetto Jameson: quando i batteri lattic:
Jameson effect: when lactic acid bacteria reach their maximum, Listeria stops growing.
The FSSP model uses it to describe competition.
Lag (fase di adattamento): il tempo in c:
Lag (adaptation phase): the time Listeria needs to adapt to the product before growing.
Without lag the estimate is more cautious.
μmax: la velocità massima di crescita (p: μmax: the maximum growth rate (per hour) in the conditions of the phase.
FSSP (Food Spoilage and Safety Predictor:
FSSP (Food Spoilage and Safety Predictor, DTU Food): growth models of Listeria and lactic acid bacteria
by Mejlholm and Dalgaard, with the Jameson effect.
Baranyi e Roberts (1994): un modello di:
Baranyi and Roberts (1994): a classic growth model, with the adaptation phase.
Here it does not use lactic acid bacteria.

σ (sigma): how much the concentration changes from one unit of the batch to another, in log10.

μ (mu): la concentrazione media del lott: μ (mu): the mean concentration of the batch, in log10 CFU/g.
